test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The salaries of X, Y, and Z are in the ratio 10 : 20 : 20. If the increments of 82%, 50%, and 19% are allowed respectively in their salaries, what will be the new ratio of their salaries?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply the **ratio parts** by their respective **percentage multipliers** (100 + increment).

New ratio → 10 × 182 : 20 × 150 : 20 × 119

Divide by 20 → 91 : 150 : 119

**∴ The correct answer is 91 : 150 : 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial ratio of salaries **X : Y : Z** = 10 : 20 : 20

**Increments:** X = 82%, Y = 50%, Z = 19%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e12327ffcfa996a2bf41c0d61ee59714fcf1a2da824965bb64a1b3b68befb5b.png] 

⇒ Let the initial salaries be 100, 200, and 200.

⇒ New salary of X = 100 + 82% of 100 = 100 + 82 = 182

⇒ New salary of Y = 200 + 50% of 200 = 200 + 100 = 300

⇒ New salary of Z = 200 + 19% of 200 = 200 + 38 = 238

⇒ New ratio = 182 : 300 : 238

⇒ Divide all terms by 2 → 91 : 150 : 119

**∴ The correct answer is 91 : 150 : 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change in Ratio

When each part of a ratio **a:b** is increased by **x%** and **y%**, the new ratio becomes **a(1 + x/100) : b(1 + y/100)**.

Base Value Selection

For easier calculation, assume ratio parts as multiples of 100 to avoid decimals during **percentage increments**.

Compound Ratio

If multiple ratios are given (A:B and B:C), they must be balanced using a **common term** before applying percentage changes.</p
